title: Tame the Hostnames
description: Replace a long ssh command line with a ~/.ssh/config host alias for the staging server.
scenario: Everyone on the team types the same 120-character ssh command for the staging box: ssh -p 2222 -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 deploy@10.20.0.5. Create a ~/.ssh/config entry so `ssh staging` does the same thing: host alias staging, HostName 10.20.0.5, user deploy, port 2222, identity file ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.
symptoms: The team shares the long ssh command in chat instead of using config files
~/.ssh/config does not exist on this box
The staging box runs sshd on port 2222, not 22
Connections must use the id_ed25519 identity, not password prompts
mission: Create ~/.ssh/config with a `Host staging` block setting HostName 10.20.0.5, User deploy, Port 2222 and IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.

hints.title: The block
hints.content: `Host staging` on its own line, then indented settings — HostName, User, Port, IdentityFile. Everything indented applies until the next Host line.

hints.title: ssh -G is the oracle
hints.content: `ssh -G staging` prints the FULL effective configuration for that alias — the definitive way to check your file without connecting anywhere.

hints.title: One alias, many settings
hints.content: The point of the alias is that `ssh staging` now carries the port, user and identity for you — no flags to misremember.

acceptance_criteria.description: the block sets User deploy, Port 2222 and an IdentityFile
